rules.name: Broken MD5 Hash Function Usage
rules.description: MD5 hash algorithm detected. MD5 is cryptographically broken due to collision and chosen-prefix attacks (Wang & Yu, 2004). Prohibited by NIST SP 800-131A Rev 2.
rules.remediation: Replace MD5 with SHA-256 / SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4) or SHA-3 (FIPS 202). For passwords, use Argon2id, PBKDF2, or bcrypt.

rules.name: Deprecated SHA-1 Hash Function Usage
rules.description: SHA-1 hash algorithm detected. SHA-1 collision resistance is broken (SHAttered attack, 2017). Deprecated for all security applications by NIST.
rules.remediation: Upgrade to SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4) or SHA3-256 (FIPS 202).

rules.name: Insecure AES Electronic Codebook (ECB) Mode
rules.description: AES in Electronic Codebook (ECB) mode detected. ECB mode encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks, preserving data patterns and leaking structural confidentiality.
rules.remediation: Immediately migrate to authenticated encryption (AEAD) such as AES-256-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D) or ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) with random initialization vectors.

rules.name: Deprecated 3DES / DES Cipher Usage
rules.description: Triple-DES or single DES cipher detected. 3DES utilizes a 64-bit block size vulnerable to Sweet32 collision attacks (CVE-2016-2183) and is formally retired by NIST SP 800-131A.
rules.remediation: Migrate data encryption to AES-256-GCM.

rules.name: Deprecated RC4 / ARC4 Stream Cipher
rules.description: RC4 stream cipher detected. RC4 contains statistical keystream biases (Bar Mitzvah, RC4 NOMORE) allowing plaintext recovery. Prohibited by RFC 7465.
rules.remediation: Replace with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

rules.name: Weak Blowfish Cipher Usage
rules.description: Blowfish cipher detected. Blowfish uses a 64-bit block size vulnerable to Sweet32 birthday attacks when encrypting large volumes of data.
rules.remediation: Upgrade to AES-256-GCM or Twofish with 128-bit block size.

rules.name: Authenticated AES-GCM Mode Detected
rules.description: AES with Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) provides high-speed Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD), ensuring both confidentiality and integrity.
rules.remediation: Maintain implementation. Ensure 96-bit unique nonces are used for each encryption operation (NIST SP 800-38D).

rules.name: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD Cipher Detected
rules.description: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD stream cipher detected. Highly secure, timing-attack resistant, and optimized for mobile/ARM architectures.
rules.remediation: Maintain implementation. Ensure nonces are never reused with the same key.

rules.name: RSA Public Key Operation & Quantum Vulnerability
rules.description: RSA public key algorithm detected. RSA relies on integer factorization hardness. While RSA-2048/3072 is classically viable through 2030, all RSA key sizes are vulnerable to polynomial-time factoring via Shor's Algorithm on Cryptanalytically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQC).
rules.remediation: Enforce key sizes >= 2048-bit (3072-bit recommended classically). Plan migration to NIST Post-Quantum FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA).

rules.name: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC / ECDSA / ECDH) Detected
rules.description: Elliptic Curve Cryptography detected (NIST P-256/384/521 or secp256k1). Strong classical security with compact keys, but completely vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on CRQC.
rules.remediation: For key exchange, implement hybrid classical + post-quantum X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203). For digital signatures, evaluate ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204).

rules.name: Ed25519 / X25519 Modern Asymmetric Crypto Detected
rules.description: Curve25519 key exchange (X25519) or digital signature (Ed25519) detected. State-of-the-art classical security and side-channel resistance; vulnerable to quantum Shor's algorithm.
rules.remediation: Deploy hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519 + ML-KEM-768).

rules.name: Diffie-Hellman / DSA Legacy Public Key Algorithm
rules.description: Classical Diffie-Hellman or DSA key establishment detected. Vulnerable to Logjam discrete log attacks if < 2048-bit, and 100% quantum-vulnerable via Shor's algorithm.
rules.remediation: Migrate to ECDH (X25519) or NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM).

rules.name: Post-Quantum Cryptography Primitive Detected (ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA)
rules.description: NIST standardized post-quantum cryptographic primitive detected (FIPS 203 Module-Lattice KEM / FIPS 204 Module-Lattice DSA). Excellent quantum resilience.
rules.remediation: Maintain implementation and monitor final NIST publication errata.

rules.name: Secure Password Hashing / KDF Detected (Argon2 / bcrypt / scrypt / PBKDF2)
rules.description: Dedicated, memory-hard or work-factored password hashing KDF detected. Resists GPU/ASIC brute-force dictionary attacks.
rules.remediation: Maintain current implementation with adequate cost factors (Argon2id: 64MB memory, 3 iterations; PBKDF2: >= 600,000 iterations per OWASP).

rules.name: Insecure / Predictable Random Number Generator (PRNG)
rules.description: Predictable pseudo-random number generator detected in security or key/token generation context. Linear Congruential Generators (LCG) allow internal state prediction.
rules.remediation: Replace with a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG): java.security.SecureRandom, secrets.token_bytes(), crypto.randomBytes(), or /dev/urandom.

rules.name: Cryptographically Secure Random Generator (CSPRNG) Detected
rules.description: Cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) detected. Provides unguessable entropy compliant with NIST SP 800-90A.
rules.remediation: Maintain implementation.

rules.name: Potential Hardcoded Cryptographic Key or Secret
rules.description: Potential hardcoded secret or cryptographic key detected directly in source/config files. Hardcoded keys can be extracted through binary reverse engineering or repository leaks.
rules.remediation: Externalize cryptographic keys to a Hardware Security Module (HSM), Cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS), or Android Keystore / StrongBox.

rules.name: Hardcoded Private Key Block in Code / Config
rules.description: Embedded X.509 / PKCS#1 / PKCS#8 private key block detected. Compromise of private key material destroys identity, authentication, and confidentiality assurances.
rules.remediation: Revoke and rotate the exposed private key immediately. Store private keys only within secure keystores / HSMs.

rules.name: Static or Zero-Filled Initialization Vector (IV / Nonce)
rules.description: Static, hardcoded, or zero-filled Initialization Vector (IV) detected. Nonce reuse in CTR, GCM, or CBC mode catastrophically destroys authenticity and enables plaintext XOR recovery.
rules.remediation: Generate a cryptographically random, unique IV for every encryption operation using a CSPRNG.

rules.name: Disabled TLS Certificate Validation / Hostname Verification
rules.description: TLS certificate validation or hostname verification explicitly disabled. Leaves network traffic vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) eavesdropping and tampering.
rules.remediation: Enable strict TLS certificate validation against trusted root CAs and enforce strict hostname checking.

rules.name: Deprecated TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1 Protocol Configuration
rules.description: Legacy TLS 1.0, 1.1, or SSL protocol detected. Vulnerable to BEAST, POODLE, and downgrade attacks. Prohibited by PCI-DSS and RFC 8996.
rules.remediation: Enforce minimum TLS 1.2 with AEAD ciphers; default to TLS 1.3.

rules.name: Android Cleartext Traffic Permitted in Manifest
rules.description: AndroidManifest.xml permits unencrypted cleartext HTTP traffic across all app network requests.
rules.remediation: Set android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and enforce HTTPS via Network Security Config.

rules.name: Android Application Debuggable Flag Enabled
rules.description: AndroidManifest.xml has android:debuggable enabled. Allows process attachment via JDWP to dump cryptographic keys and runtime memory.
rules.remediation: Ensure android:debuggable is false in release builds.

rules.name: Hardware-Backed Keystore / KMS Integration Detected
rules.description: Hardware-backed key storage (Android Keystore StrongBox, AWS KMS HSM, Vault, or PKCS#11) detected. Keys remain non-exportable and protected in secure enclaves.
rules.remediation: Maintain implementation and enforce key rotation policies.

rules.name: Weak RSA Key Size (< 2048-bit) Detected
rules.description: RSA key size below 2048-bit threshold detected. Keys under 2048-bit provide inadequate classical security (< 112 bits) and are easily factorable.
rules.remediation: Upgrade key size immediately to at least 2048-bit (3072-bit recommended). Plan PQC transition to ML-KEM/ML-DSA.
